faq.q: How long does a 1-metre pendulum take to swing?
faq.a: About 2 seconds for a full swing there and back, or 1 second each way. That is why a pendulum of about 1 metre, called a seconds pendulum, was used in many tall clocks.

faq.q: Why does a short pendulum swing faster?
faq.a: A short pendulum travels round a smaller arc, so it finishes each swing sooner. The time grows with the square root of the length, so four times the length gives twice the time.
asks: Why does a shorter string make a pendulum faster?

faq.q: Does the weight of the bob matter?
faq.a: No. A heavier bob is pulled harder by gravity but is also harder to speed up, and the two effects cancel. Only the length, and the strength of gravity, set the timing.
asks: Does a heavy pendulum swing faster?

faq.q: Would a pendulum swing differently on the Moon?
faq.a: Yes, more slowly. The Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's, so a pendulum there takes about two and a half times as long for each swing.
asks: How does gravity change a pendulum?

faq.q: Why do people with long legs walk more slowly?
faq.a: When you walk, each leg swings forward like a pendulum. Longer legs swing more slowly, so tall people and long-legged animals naturally take slower but longer strides.

facts: A pendulum about 99.4 centimetres long takes 1 second for each one-way swing, 2 seconds there and back.
Christiaan Huygens built the first pendulum clock in 1656.
